newsitem.title: USA: Investors won't abandon stocks, fund executive says.
newsitem.headline: Investors won't abandon stocks, fund executive says.

text.p: Mutual fund investors will not be the cause of any future bear market in U.S. stocks, said a top fund industry executive Tuesday.
"I don't think it's logical to (conclude) that mutual fund shareholders will be the cause of the next bear market," Don Powell, chairman of the Investment Co Institute (ICI) said.
Powell said he did not expect that redemptions by U.S. fund investors would lead to a bear market. "There is no evidence of a run of mutual funds in any of the past 14 bear markets," Powell said.

Powell said he believes rational investor behavior will continue in the future. "I have no sense that they are not going to continue to act rationally looking forward," Powell said at a press briefing here.
Powell said that a look at past bear markets indicated that redemptions did not increase and in some cases there was a slight increase in net new sales.
Matthew Fink, president of the trade group, said he expected that the Securities and Exchange Commission would propose a new shorter fund prospectus within the next month.
The profile prospectus will be only two to three pages long and contain simple language to explain the basis of the fund.
Fink said he did not support a ratings systems for bond fund prospectuses because he was concerned that they might not always accurately reflect the risks of funds portfolio of securities.
Fink urged the SEC to step-up enforcement of existing laws concerning the use of soft dollars, or the exchange of goods and service for the funds trading business.
Fink said the laws "ought to be enforced" in any cases where money managers improperly received soft dollars in return for steering stock trading to a investment firm or brokerage.
